About Joe

### It's Just Me. That's the Point.

I spent years inside the roofing industry — watching owners and investors enter the business to make money without actually knowing the work. They'd promise smooth jobs and zero issues, then lean on sales reps and project managers to handle everything. The homeowner paid for that overhead and still got inconsistency.

I started No Big Deal because I know the work, I know insurance restoration, and I wanted to be the person who actually handles it — not the person who delegates it. Coming up on 7 years in this trade. I learned what works and what doesn't in the field, not in a training room.

Straight Answers

### Questions Homeowners Actually Ask

No fine print, no runaround — just honest answers to what people want to know before they call.

How much does a new roof cost in the Cincinnati area?

It depends on your roof's size, pitch, and the shingle you pick — but to give you a real number: most architectural-shingle replacements in Greater Cincinnati run about $665–$745 per roofing square installed, with budget and premium tiers landing roughly $610–$825 per square. Our free Instant Estimate gives you a tailored ballpark in about 60 seconds — no phone call, no pressure.

Do you offer financing?

Yes — through Acorn Finance, a lending marketplace that lets you check your options with a soft credit pull that doesn't affect your credit score. You'll see the actual lender, rate, and full terms before you commit to anything. If financing isn't the right move for your project, Joe will tell you straight.

Can you help with a storm damage insurance claim?

Absolutely — insurance restoration is one of the things we handle most. We document the damage properly, walk you through the claim, and meet your adjuster on the roof so you're not stuck translating roofing jargon. You focus on your deductible; we handle the rest.

What areas do you serve?

We cover Greater Cincinnati — across Southwest Ohio and into Kentucky. Cincinnati, Milford, Loveland, Mason, Batavia, West Chester and the surrounding communities are all areas I work regularly, and as of 2026 I also serve the Lexington area — Lexington, Georgetown, Nicholasville, Winchester, Richmond, and Versailles — on scheduled trips. Not sure if you're in range? Just call Joe and ask.

Are you licensed, insured, and certified?

Yes — No Big Deal is licensed and insured, and we're factory-certified by the biggest names in roofing: GAF (GAF Certified) and TAMKO (Pro Gold). Those certifications unlock the strongest manufacturer warranties available — and you can verify each one directly with the manufacturer. On siding, I'm a member of the James Hardie Alliance. And as of 2026, No Big Deal is certified Locally Owned & Operated by American Operator — one local owner, not a franchise.

What actually happens when I call?

You get Joe — not a call center, not a salesperson reading a script. Tell him what's going on and he'll give you a straight answer, usually the same day. If you need an inspection, he'll set one up. No pressure, no obligation, no runaround — that's kind of the whole point.

Still have a question? Call Joe directly at (859) 420-7382 — he answers.

The Honest Version

### Why "No Big Deal" Actually Means Something.

Where I'm from first, because it explains a lot. I grew up in eastern Kentucky, fifteen minutes from the Red River Gorge — the kind of place where you learn to fix things yourself, because nobody's coming to fix them for you. I lived in Lexington after that, did a stretch out in Omaha, Nebraska, then moved to Cincinnati, found the roofing trade, and never left. Kentucky roots, Midwest miles, Cincinnati home.

I spent years inside the roofing industry — working for companies, watching how it all operates from the inside. And I saw the same problem over and over: owners and investors enter this business to make money without actually knowing the work. They promise smooth jobs and zero issues, then lean on sales reps, project managers, and whoever they can hire cheap to actually handle the roofs.

The result? A lot of those jobs end up nightmares. The salesperson who sold your job isn't the person showing up to do it. The person showing up doesn't know your situation, doesn't know what was promised, and is moving on to the next roof before yours is done right. And the homeowner has no recourse — they just wanted their roof fixed.

I started No Big Deal Home Solutions because I wanted to do it differently. Every customer I take on gets my personal attention — from the first call to the final walkthrough. I know their name, I know their situation, and I care about the outcome because my reputation is literally what I'm selling.

"No Big Deal" isn't me downplaying the work. It's a promise: whatever problem you're dealing with — a hail-damaged roof, an insurance adjuster missing half the damage, a leak you can't figure out — I've seen it before, and I'll document it, explain it, and fix it. No big deal.

Experience

### 7+ Years in the Trenches. Here's What That Actually Means.

🌩️

Insurance Restoration

I've worked hundreds of insurance claims — storm, hail, wind, fire, water. I know how adjusters think, where claims get undervalued, and how to document damage so you get what you're actually owed.

📋

Xactimate Estimating

Xactimate is the industry-standard software insurance companies use to price claims. I know it inside and out — which means I speak the same language as your adjuster and can document the line items that get missed.

🏠

Full Exterior Scope

Roofing, siding, gutters, fascia, soffit, decking, flashing — I handle the complete exterior. I'm a GAF® Certified Contractor and install the full GAF system on GAF roofs, which unlocks enhanced manufacturer warranty coverage on top of The Pledge on my workmanship.

💬

Direct Communication

I give every client my number. Not a company line — my number. I respond to texts and calls personally throughout the project. If something comes up, you're not filing a ticket. You're texting me.

Brand Picks

### Why I Install What I Install.

I don't get sponsorship money to promote any brand. Every product on my roofs earned its spot the hard way — through years of watching what fails at year 7 and what's still holding up at year 20. Here's where I landed:

GAF

GAF Shingles + Master Flow Pivot Boots

My default shingle line (Timberline NS / HDZ / UHDZ) with the most coherent warranty system in the industry, and their all-metal Pivot Pipe Boot is the only commercial boot I've seen that completely eliminates the rubber-gasket failure that kills normal roofs at year 10. Read my take →

TAMKO

TAMKO Impact-Resistant Shingles

The Lifetime Pledge

### No Big Deal. Seriously, it's in the name.

My name is Joe Deal. The company is No Big Deal Home Solutions. That's not a coincidence. Every roof, every siding job, every gutter run, every storm claim I take on is built on one promise — that working with us should be the smoothest, most straightforward experience your house ever has. Now and for as long as you own it.

Read the Pledge →
Call Joe — (859) 420-7382

Picking a roof?
The Pledge applies to every roof I build. See the three tiers — The NBD Guarantee →

The Origin

### Why I built it this way.

Before No Big Deal, I sold for the companies you've heard of. The ones with the trucks, the radio spots, the decades on the sign out front. The companies homeowners assume will do good work because the name is everywhere.

Here's what I learned, sitting at hundreds of kitchen tables: people weren't picking those companies because of those companies. They were picking them because of the conversation — because of the relationship I'd built sitting across from them. They were buying me. The sign on the truck just made it feel safer.

And then the work would happen. And sometimes it'd be great. And sometimes it'd be a hassle — a missed appointment, a sloppy crew, a phone call that didn't get returned, a punch-list item that lingered for months. I'd hear the same kind of sentence over and over from people I'd already shaken hands with:

"They're a big company. I really thought this was going to be no big deal for them. Man… it was a hassle."
— Said to me, more times than I can count

That sentence is why this company exists. I got tired of being the relationship that bigger companies were borrowing. I wanted the relationship to be the company. So I started this one — and I literally named it after the experience I wanted you to have.

"No Big Deal" isn't a slogan I dreamed up in a marketing meeting. It's the standard. It's the bar. It's what every person on the job, every estimate I write, every phone call I take is measured against. Was it a big deal? Then I didn't do my job. Was it no big deal? Then we did it right.

The Promise

### The Lifetime Pledge.

Most contractors disappear once the check clears. The number stops working. The truck stops coming back. The "warranty" turns into voicemail.

I don't.

For as long as I'm in business and you own this home, you can call me about anything I worked on — and I'll come look. No charge to diagnose. No charge to give you a straight answer.

If I caused the problem, I make it right under whatever warranty applies to that job. If something else caused it — weather, age, another contractor's work, a tree your neighbor finally pruned five years too late — I'll tell you exactly what's going on, and quote the fix fairly if you want me to handle it. No pressure. No upsell. No runaround.

That's the Pledge. It's not free repairs forever — that wouldn't be honest, and you'd see right through it. It's something better: you'll always know what's wrong with your house, you'll always get a straight answer, and you'll never get ducked.

Reactive vs. proactive — two different things: The Pledge is reactive: you call, I come. Forever, on every job. The Elite tier of the NBD Guarantee adds something different — a proactive piece, where I reach out to you every year, walk the roof on your behalf, and send you a written report. The Pledge is the always-included foundation under every job I do. Elite is the only tier where I also put the calendar reminder on my side.

— Joe Deal
Owner & Operator

Why I Can Stand Behind It

### A pledge is only as good as what's behind it.

I can promise to come back forever because I'm careful about what I install in the first place. I work with manufacturers and partners I'd trust on my own house — and I install to their spec, every time, so the materials actually do what they're supposed to do.

The full breakdown of which manufacturers, which products, and which warranty paperwork ride along with each tier of roof lives on the Guarantee page — that's where it belongs.

For roofs:
See The NBD Guarantee → — Standard, Preferred, Elite. Materials, components, and warranty paperwork compared.

In Practice

### What "no big deal" actually looks like.

A pledge is words. Here's what those words translate to on the day a crew is on your roof — because the experience is the promise.

- The phone gets answered.Same number, same person. Before the job, during the job, ten years after the job.
- You know when we're showing up.A real arrival window, communicated the day before. If something changes, you hear about it from me first.
- Photos before, photos after.You see what we found, you see what we did. No "trust us" — just receipts.
- The site is cleaner than we found it.Magnetic sweeps for nails, full debris haul-away. Your kids and dogs go back outside without thinking about it.
- Walkthrough before the balance is due.We don't ask for the final payment until you've walked the work and approved it. Out loud. With me standing there.
- Documentation that's actually useful.Written warranty, manufacturer paperwork on materials, insurance certificate on request. Saved in our system so we can pull your file in 30 seconds, years later.

Two Layers Of Standing Behind The Work

### The Pledge is the relationship. Each job has its own paperwork.

I want to be precise about this, because vague warranty language is one of the things I built this company to get away from. Every job we do is covered two different ways — and they do two different things.

Layer 1 · Per Job

#### A Written Warranty & Agreement.

Every estimate spells out exactly what's covered and exactly what isn't. Lifetime workmanship coverage, manufacturer warranties on materials, scope of the work, what triggers a re-visit. You'll see all of it in writing before you sign anything. No fine print. No "ask me later."

Layer 2 · Forever

#### The Lifetime Pledge.

Sits on top of every job. The Pledge is the promise that whenever you call — whether or not the issue turns out to be something a written warranty covers — I'll still come look, I won't charge you to look, and you'll still get the truth about what's going on with your house. Covered by warranty, I fix it. Not our work, I'll quote the fix fairly. Either way, you get a straight answer, not a runaround.

Real Questions

### The questions skeptics ask. Good — they should.

I'd rather you read these than wonder. If your question isn't here, text me — I'll answer it.

So what does "lifetime" actually mean? Free repairs forever?

No — and I want to be straight about that, because "lifetime" is a word a lot of contractors throw around dishonestly. The Lifetime Pledge means lifetime diagnosis and a lifetime straight answer: as long as I'm in business and you own the home, you can call about anything I worked on, I'll come look at it, I won't charge you to look, and I'll tell you exactly what's going on. If it's something I caused and it's covered by your job's written warranty, I fix it. If it's not, I'll quote the fix fairly. The Pledge is the relationship — not a blank check.

What if it turns out the problem isn't your work?

You still get the diagnosis for free. That's the whole point. A lot of homeowners get burned because no contractor will tell them what's going on without a sales pitch attached. I'll come look, I'll show you what I find, and I'll tell you whether it's something I should fix, something a different specialist should fix, or something you don't need to spend money on at all. If you want me to handle it, I'll quote it. If you want to shop the quote or wait, that's completely fine.

What if it's twenty years from now and you're not in business anymore?

Honest answer — I can't guarantee a phone call from someone who doesn't exist. Nobody can. What I can guarantee is that for as long as I am in business, the Pledge holds. And that the materials I install are from manufacturers (like GAF and Norandex) whose warranties are tied to the product and the home, not to me personally. So even in the worst case, the manufacturer paperwork is yours regardless of what happens to my company. That's part of why I'm careful about which manufacturers I install in the first place.

What if I sell the house?

The job's written warranty has its own transferability terms — some manufacturer warranties transfer once to a new owner and add real resale value, and we'll spell that out specifically on your paperwork. The Pledge itself is between me and whoever owns the home — so if you sell, the new owner inherits the same right to call me about that work. Tell them about it; it's a real selling point.

Does the Pledge cost extra? Is it built into the price?

The Pledge is included on every job — it's not an add-on, it's not a premium tier, and there's no separate line item for it. The reason it doesn't cost extra is that it's not really a product. It's just how I run the company. Picking up the phone is free. Driving over to look at something is mostly free. Being honest costs nothing at all.

What kinds of work does this apply to?

Everything we do — roofing, siding, gutters, and storm-damage insurance restoration. Whether we put a full roof on your house or wrapped one fascia board on a left gable, the Pledge applies.

How do I actually use it later? Do I need a card or a code or something?

Just call (859) 420-7382 with your name and address. We pull your file in our system, see exactly what we did and when, and schedule a time for me to come look. No portal logins, no warranty registration websites, no proof-of-purchase scavenger hunt. That's the entire process.

If we're a fit, great. If we're not, you'll still walk away knowing more about your house than you did before I showed up.

Real Talk From Joe

#### Three tiers because three roofs deserve three answers.

I get it — three tiers can feel like a sales gimmick. So here's the actual truth: I built three tiers because three different homeowners walked into my life with three different roofs, and the same answer didn't fit all three.

The retired couple selling in two years to downsize doesn't need Elite. It would be wasted money. I'd put Standard on that roof and sleep fine. The young family in their forever home with a baby coming? That's where I push Preferred — better warranty, transferable to the eventual buyer, premium pipe boots that won't leak in year 7. The third group — the ones who tell me "this is the last roof I'm ever buying on this house" — that's Elite. Visible LumaNail fasteners so I can prove I did it right, me reaching out every year on the calendar to walk the roof and send them a report, my name on a certificate. They want to be done thinking about it.

None of this is upsell. The tier you should pick is the one that actually fits your situation. If you're getting pressure to go higher than what your honest answer says, that's not me — that's a contractor trying to hit a number.

### Common Questions.

Why three tiers instead of one quote?

Because not every roof should be the same. A rental that's getting sold in 5 years doesn't need the Elite tier. A forever home does. Three tiers means the right roof for your situation, not the most expensive one I can sell you.

Can I mix and match between tiers?

Some of it, yes. The shingle grade is the spine of each tier — that doesn't mix. But individual upgrades like LumaNail or upgraded pipe boots can be added to a lower tier as a la carte if it's important to you. Ask Joe at the inspection.

What GAF warranty coverage do I get?

Joe is a GAF® Certified Contractor, which makes enhanced manufacturer warranty coverage (including System Plus) available on qualifying full-system installs. The warranty registered at install time is what applies — once it's on the paperwork, that's the contract. The NBD Lifetime Pledge — Joe coming back personally — is independent of GAF and applies forever regardless.

Why isn't there a "different shingle brand" tier (Owens Corning, Atlas, CertainTeed)?

Honest answer: I install GAF because GAF's warranty system, install training, and accessory product line are the most coherent and best-supported in this market. I'm not going to pretend I'm equally fluent in every brand just to give you a brand-choice illusion. If you specifically want Owens Corning or another brand, talk to me — I'll tell you straight whether I think that's a good call for your roof.

Can I add LumaNail to a Standard or Preferred roof?

LumaNail is bundled into Elite. If you want it on a Standard or Preferred build, ask me and I'll work it into the bundle as a make-or-break upgrade — but I don't lead with it as an upcharge. Read about LumaNail → GAF Timberline Lineup

Why don't you publish exact tier prices?

Because every roof is different — pitch, square count, decking condition, accessibility, tear-off complexity, insurance documentation. Relative pricing is honest: Preferred is roughly 9% over Standard, Elite is roughly 21% over Standard. Exact numbers come from a free in-person estimate where I actually look at your roof.

What's the proactive annual outreach on Elite — how does that actually work?

It's written into the Elite contract. The reminder is on my calendar, not yours. Every year I call you, schedule a 20-minute roof check, get up there, photograph anything notable, and send you a one-page written report. No charge, no upsell, for the life of the roof. That's the difference between Elite and the lower tiers: every NBD roof has The Pledge (you can always call me), but only Elite has me reaching out to you on a schedule.

### Ready to pick a tier?

Free in-person estimate. I'll walk your roof, talk through which tier actually fits your situation, and give you a written number. No pressure, no commission salesperson, no markup.

## The NBD Build — Premium Roof Components System | No Big Deal

What makes Elite, Elite · A bundle inside The NBD Guarantee

### The standard equipment on Elite.

The NBD Build is three premium components bundled standard into every Elite-tier roof — and available à-la-carte on Standard or Preferred. Each one solves a specific failure mode I've watched destroy "good" roofs early: invisible fasteners, cracking pipe boots, plastic exhaust caps. Not because they look good in a brochure. Because I've torn off enough roofs to know where they go wrong.

Compare All Three Tiers →
See the three components

The Three Failure Modes

### Three things every roof fails on first.

Not shingles. Not warranty paperwork. These three. They're invisible from the curb until the leak shows up — and they're standard equipment on every Elite-tier roof I build. Lower tiers can pull any of the three à-la-carte.

01

Failure mode #1 · Invisible nails

#### The fastener you can't see is the one that failed.

NBD answers it with: LumaNail™

Standard galvanized nails are bare metal — once driven, they're invisible. An underdriven nail, an overdriven nail, a missed nail strip — all impossible to verify. One bad nail in a wind event and you lose the shingle. Sometimes the row above it too. LumaNail makes every install error visible in real time, before the next course covers it.

Read about LumaNail → GAF Timberline Lineup

02

Failure mode #2 · Cracking pipe boots

#### The neoprene boot dies at year 7-12. Always.

NBD answers it with: GAF Master Flow Pivot Boot on Preferred & Elite

Standard neoprene pipe boots crack from UV exposure within 7-12 years. When they fail, water runs straight down the plumbing vent stack into your bathroom. The Pivot Boot is GAF's all-metal solution: ball-and-socket pivot, no rubber to UV-cook, no parts to fail. It's standard on Preferred and Elite. Standard tier ships the serviceable Roofivent iVent Pipe Flashing — also a lifetime-functionality unit, just a different design.

Read about Pivot Boot →

03

Failure mode #3 · Quiet exhaust failures

#### Your bath fan vent cap is plastic and 8 years old.

NBD answers it with: Roofivent iVent ECO (Preferred & Elite)

Standard bath/kitchen/dryer exhaust roof caps are thin plastic with a flap that warps, sticks, or breaks within a decade. The result: condensation in the attic, a mold problem nobody connects to the cause. iVent ECO is a polypropylene unit with a built-in condensation drain and a serviceable rubber gasket. It vents the appliance and drains the moisture. Both jobs.

Read about Roofivent →

### The bundle, not the brochure.

"Premium roof" almost always means premium shingle — and nobody talks about the parts that actually go wrong first. The NBD Build is the bundle that answers that gap. Three components, three failure modes, no marketing fluff.

On Elite, all three are standard equipment — that's what makes Elite, Elite. On Standard or Preferred, any of the three can be added à-la-carte if it matters to your specific situation; ask Joe at the inspection.

"The shingle is the part you can see from the street. The fastener, the pipe boot, and the exhaust cap are the parts that decide whether your shingle stays attached."

The Build × The Tiers

### Elite is the only tier where the whole Build ships in the box.

Each component below shows up where it actually fits. The full Build — all three together — is what you get on Elite by default. Lower tiers get the components that solve the failure modes most likely on your specific house.

★ Standard equipment

"Standard equipment" means it's already in the price — you don't ask for it, it's there. "À-la-carte" means it can be added to a lower tier as a line item if it matters for your specific roof.

Or call Joe — (859) 420-7382

If you're not on Elite

### When à-la-carte actually makes sense.

Most homeowners on Standard or Preferred don't need the full Build — that's why Elite exists. But if one of these three situations is your situation, pulling a single component à-la-carte is the right call. Tell me at the inspection.

Scenario 01

#### You're on Standard, but the bath fan has leaked before.

Your existing exhaust caps are 8+ years old, the plastic is brittle, and you've already had attic moisture issues. The shingle isn't the problem — the cap is.

Pull à-la-carte: Roofivent iVent ECO ($)

Scenario 02

#### You're on Preferred, but you live where the wind hits hard.

Open lots, unprotected ridges, or a recent neighbor lost shingles in a storm. Pivot Boot and iVent ECO are already standard on Preferred. The piece you're missing is fastener verifiability.

Pull à-la-carte: LumaNail™ ($$)

Scenario 03

#### You want all three but the budget says Standard.

Honest answer: at that point, look hard at Preferred. The math usually works out closer than you think because you're already paying for the GAF Pivot upgrade and the iVent ECO upgrade à-la-carte. Preferred bundles them at lower marginal cost.

Probably pick: Preferred (full upgrade, +9% over Standard)

### Full Roof Replacement Done Right the First Time

A roof replacement is one of the biggest investments a homeowner makes — and it's also one of the most common jobs where homeowners get taken advantage of. Joe Deal started No Big Deal Home Solutions specifically because he was tired of watching big companies charge $18,000 for jobs that cost $6,000.

When you call Joe for a roof replacement in Cincinnati or the surrounding area, he shows up personally. He gets on the roof. He gives you a straight honest assessment of what needs to happen — and what doesn't. If repair is the right call instead of replacement, he'll tell you that too.

Every roof replacement starts with a complete tear-off — I don't layer new shingles over old ones and call it a day. I pull everything, inspect the decking, replace any damaged boards, install fresh underlayment, and then install your new shingles using GAF Timberline products — or TAMKO impact-resistant shingles for hail country — carrying a lifetime manufacturer shingle warranty. Weighing 3-tab against architectural? Joe's honest breakdown of the real cost difference covers when the upgrade is worth it — and when it isn't.

If your roof was damaged by storm, hail, or wind, I document everything and meet your adjuster on the roof. Most homeowners have never been through a claim — I explain every step, and the claim stays yours.

- Complete tear-off & debris disposal — nothing left behind

- GAF Timberline or TAMKO impact-resistant shingles — your choice of style & color

Questions & Answers

### Roof Replacement FAQ

How long does a roof replacement take?

Most residential roof replacements in Cincinnati are completed in one day. Larger homes or complex rooflines may take two days. I don't leave a job unfinished — your roof will be weathertight every night regardless.

Does my homeowner's insurance cover a roof replacement?

If your roof was damaged by storm, hail, or wind, there's a good chance your insurance covers it. Ohio homeowners are often surprised how much their policy covers once it's properly documented. Joe will inspect your roof, document the damage, and tell you honestly whether you have a claim worth filing — before you do anything else.

What shingles do you use?

I install GAF Timberline shingles as my default lineup — carrying a lifetime limited manufacturer warranty on the materials. I carry architectural (dimensional) shingles as my standard and can also install TAMKO's impact-resistant shingles, including HailGuard, the first asphalt shingle with a hail warranty, which may qualify for insurance discounts in Ohio.

Do you tear off the old roof or go over it?

I always do a full tear-off. Layering new shingles over old ones is faster and cheaper for the contractor, but it hides problems in the decking, adds unnecessary weight, and voids most manufacturer warranties. I don't cut corners like that.

How much does a roof replacement cost in Cincinnati?

Every roof is different — size, pitch, material, and condition of the decking all affect the price. What I can promise is that my quotes are fair and I'll explain every line item. Call Joe and get a real number, not a range designed to anchor your expectations high. And if the honest number is more than this month's budget, that's what financing is for — spread it into a monthly payment through the Acorn Finance marketplace, with a soft credit pull to see real offers that never touches your score.

Do you serve areas outside of Cincinnati?

Yes — I serve Greater Cincinnati including Milford, Loveland, Mason, Batavia, Lebanon, Maineville, Blue Ash, Indian Hill, Amelia, and surrounding communities. If you're not sure I cover your area, just call or text me.

Questions & Answers

### Roof Repair FAQ

How quickly can you get out for a leaking roof?

I respond fast — especially for active leaks. Call or text me directly and I'll get eyes on it as soon as possible, often same day or next day depending on location and time of year.

Can you match my existing shingles for a repair?

I do my best to match color and style as closely as possible. If your roof is newer, I can often get an exact match from the same manufacturer. On older roofs, shingles fade over time and a perfect match isn't always possible — I'll show you what's available before any work starts.

How do I know if I need repair or full replacement?

That's exactly what Joe's inspection answers. General rule of thumb: if your roof is under 15 years old and the damage is isolated, repair usually makes sense. Over 20 years old with widespread issues, replacement is often more cost-effective long-term. Joe will lay out the honest pros and cons for your specific situation.

Does insurance cover roof repairs?

If the damage was caused by a covered event — storm, hail, wind, falling debris — your homeowner's insurance likely covers the repair. Joe will document everything and explain how the claim process works.

Do you fix roofs on commercial buildings?

Yes — full commercial, not just light commercial. My roofing crew repairs and replaces flat and low-slope roofs in EPDM and TPO, apartment complexes and multi-family buildings, and small-business buildings, and I'm on every job myself. See my Commercial Roofing page for the details and real commercial jobs, or give me a call to talk about your building.

Storm Damage & Insurance

### Storm Damage Handled Start to Finish

When a storm hits, most homeowners don't know where to start. They call their insurance company, get a claim number, wait for an adjuster, and hope the payout covers the damage. That process goes a lot better when you have someone in your corner who does this every week.

Joe Deal has worked alongside insurance adjusters on hundreds of storm damage claims in Greater Cincinnati. He knows what adjusters look for, how to document damage thoroughly, and how to make sure nothing legitimate gets missed or undervalued in the initial inspection. That documentation makes a real difference in what your claim pays.

I handle roof, siding, and gutter storm damage — often all three on the same home after a major hail or wind event. Emergency tarping is available for active roof leaks while the claim process works through. I work with all major insurance carriers operating in Ohio.

- Full damage inspection — roof, siding, gutters, and soft metals
- Thorough photo and measurement documentation for claim filing
- Insurance adjuster meeting on site
- Supplement documentation for missed or undervalued damage items
- Emergency tarping for active roof leaks (available 7 days)
- Full roof replacement if warranted by damage extent
- Impact-rated shingle options for hail country — GAF Timberline or TAMKO's impact-resistant shingles (incl. HailGuard, the first asphalt shingle with a hail warranty)
- Siding replacement or repair for hail and wind damage
- Seamless gutter replacement for storm-damaged gutters
- Work with all major Ohio insurance carriers

What Homeowners Say

### Straight Talk From Real People

Questions & Answers

### Storm Damage & Insurance FAQ

Do I need to file a claim before calling you?

No — call Joe first. He'll inspect the damage and tell you honestly whether you have a claim worth filing. Filing unnecessarily can affect your rates, so it's worth knowing what you're working with before you contact your insurer.

How soon after a storm should I get my roof inspected?

As soon as possible. Insurance policies have claim filing deadlines, and documentation is always stronger while the damage is fresh. If you had a major storm in your area, call Joe and get on the schedule.

What does your storm inspection cover?

I inspect the full exterior — roof field, ridgeline, flashing, gutters, downspouts, siding, windows, AC unit top, and any other impact-susceptible surfaces. I'm looking for hail strikes, wind damage, and impact marks that adjusters need to see.

What if the insurance adjuster's estimate is lower than your repair estimate?

This happens. I can supplement the claim — which means providing documentation and line-item support for damage that was missed or undervalued in the adjuster's estimate. The insurance company isn't always wrong, but they're also not always thorough.

What insurance companies do you work with?

I work with all major carriers operating in Ohio — State Farm, Nationwide, Grange, Erie, Allstate, Progressive, and others. The process is similar regardless of carrier.

Is storm damage restoration covered by my deductible?

Your deductible applies to any insurance claim, regardless of the repair type — and it's yours to pay. No contractor can legally waive, absorb, or cover your deductible for you; anyone who offers to is committing insurance fraud that can put your claim at risk. Joe does it the honest way — he documents every bit of damage and fights for the full, legitimate payout, so your out-of-pocket stays as low as it honestly can.

Hail & Wind Damage

### Your Insurance Company Has a Team Working Against You. Now You Have Joe.

Most homeowners look at their roof after a storm and think everything looks fine. It's not. Hail damage hides. It bruises the mat under the granules, cracks the asphalt, and compromises the seal strip — and your insurance company is counting on you not knowing that.

Joe Deal has been doing insurance restoration work in Greater Cincinnati for over 7 years. He knows exactly what adjusters look for, what they try to underpay, and how to document damage so your claim gets approved for what it actually should be.

Here's the deal: You call Joe. He comes out, gets on your roof, and does a real inspection — not a 10-minute walkthrough. He documents every hit, every cracked shingle, every damaged soft metal. He builds the file. He meets the adjuster. He writes the supplement if the initial payout is short. You make one decision at the end — do you want to move forward or not.

Common Questions

### What Homeowners Ask About Hail Claims.

Will filing a claim raise my insurance rates?

In Ohio, insurance companies cannot raise your rates for a single weather-related claim — it's an act of nature, not negligence. That said, every policy is different. Joe will tell you upfront if your deductible situation makes filing worth it or not.

My neighbor got their roof done — does that mean I have damage too?

Often yes, but not always. Hail damage depends on which direction the storm came from, the pitch of your roof, and the age of your shingles. Joe will give you an honest answer — if there's no viable claim, he'll tell you that too.

How long do I have to file a hail damage claim in Ohio?

Most Ohio policies allow 1-2 years from the date of loss. However, waiting too long makes the documentation harder and adjusters more skeptical. If you had a storm in the last 18 months, call Joe now and find out what you're working with.

What if my claim gets denied?

Denials get appealed. I document everything specifically so there's a paper trail. If the initial denial is bogus, there are options — including Ohio's appraisal process. He's been through this before.

Emergency Roof Tarping

### A Tarp Isn't the Repair. It's What Saves the Repair.

When wind peels shingles back or a limb opens the decking, the water that follows usually does more damage than the storm did. Insulation, drywall, ceilings, floors — that's where the real money bleeds. A properly installed tarp stops the bleeding the day it happens. And if water already got through, my interior crew handles the drywall and ceiling repair once the roof is fixed.

Here's the part most homeowners don't know: nearly every policy carries a duty to mitigate — after a storm, you're expected to take reasonable steps to keep the damage from getting worse. Emergency tarping is exactly that step, and when the damage is part of a covered claim, reasonable mitigation costs are routinely part of the claim. I photograph the damage before the tarp goes down and after it's secured, so your file is built from hour one.

And I'll say the quiet part out loud: a tarp is temporary. It's a bridge to the real repair or replacement — not a substitute for it. I install it like it matters, because it does. Then you get a straight plan for what comes next, and if insurance is in play, I document the damage and meet your adjuster when they come out.

- Same-day / next-morning response for active leaks — 7 days a week
- Heavy-duty tarps, anchored to shed water — not a bedsheet and a prayer
- Photo documentation before and after, formatted for your claim file
- Wind, hail, and fallen-limb damage — roof, ridge, and valley coverage
- Storm claim? I document the damage and meet your adjuster
- Straight answer on what comes next: repair, replacement, or wait

One of my tarps, from my drone: cap-nailed in tight rows, seated under the damaged eave so water sheds over it — not a brick-weighted bedsheet. The fastening is the whole job.

FAQ

### Tarping Questions. Straight Answers.

How fast can you get a tarp on my roof?

Active leaks jump the line — call or text me directly and say water's coming in. Same-day when weather and daylight allow, first thing next morning otherwise. Seven days a week.

Does insurance pay for emergency tarping?

When the damage is part of a covered claim, reasonable emergency mitigation — tarping included — is routinely part of the claim, because your policy expects you to prevent further damage. I photograph everything before and after so the cost is easy for your adjuster to see and approve. If the damage isn't covered, you get the price before I climb — no surprises either way.

Will the tarp itself damage my roof?

Installed right, no — that's the point of calling someone who does roofs for a living. I anchor tarps to shed water and hold in wind while keeping new penetrations to the minimum the situation allows, and anything the installation touches is part of the permanent repair plan. A tarp flapping loose does more harm than good, which is why "installed right" matters.

How long can a tarp stay on a roof?

Weeks, not seasons. Tarps weather, UV breaks them down, and winter is hard on them. Think of it as a bridge that buys you time to do the repair correctly — the plan for the permanent fix starts the same day the tarp goes down.

Can you tarp it AND document it for my insurance claim?

That's exactly why you'd call me instead of a tarp-only crew. I'm versed in insurance restoration — I tarp it, document it for your claim, write the estimate, and meet your adjuster when they come out. One person, the whole way. It's vastly different from retail roofing, and it's what I do.

Questions & Answers

### Commercial Roofing FAQ

Do you actually do commercial roofing, or just houses?

Yes, full commercial — not just a small flat section on the back of a house. My roofing crew does flat and low-slope roofs in EPDM and TPO, multi-building apartment complexes, and small-business buildings. The By Golly’s rebuild in Milford and the apartment complex in West Liberty, KY on my Our Work page are both commercial jobs, with photos and price ranges.

What kinds of commercial roofs do you work on?

Flat and low-slope roofs in EPDM (rubber) and TPO, plus shingle roofs on apartment complexes and other multi-family buildings. That covers small-business buildings like restaurants and storefronts, and the low-slope sections a lot of mixed buildings carry. If you’re not sure what’s on your roof, that’s what the inspection is for — I’ll tell you what it is and what shape it’s in.

Who does the work on a commercial job?

An established roofing crew I bring in — independent subcontractors who carry their own insurance. I’m on every job myself: I do the inspection, write the scope, and I’m there while the work happens. You deal with me from the first call to the final walkthrough, not a salesman who hands you off.

Can you keep my business open while the roof gets fixed?

That’s the goal, and I plan the work around it. On By Golly’s in Milford, that meant a same-day tarp so the kitchen could stay open, then the full tear-off and new EPDM once the real fix was scheduled. What’s possible depends on the building and the scope, and I’ll tell you straight what to expect before we start.

Do you handle apartment complexes and multi-family buildings?

Yes. One of the jobs on my Our Work page is a multi-building apartment complex in West Liberty, KY — every building torn off down to the decking, new synthetic underlayment, architectural shingles, new ridge vents, and all flashing replaced, drone-documented start to finish for the property management company. If you manage a property, I’ll work with you or your management company directly.

Are your GAF and TAMKO certifications for commercial roofs?

No, and I won’t dress them up as if they were. GAF Certified and TAMKO Pro Gold are residential shingle programs. What I can show you on commercial is the actual work — real jobs with photos and price ranges on my Our Work page. Whatever goes on your roof, the product and the paperwork that comes with it are written into the scope before you sign.

Will insurance cover storm damage on a commercial roof?

Sometimes — it depends on your commercial property policy and what caused the damage. The Milford job started with wind damage. If a storm is behind your leak, I document it the same way I do for a homeowner’s claim, so you and your adjuster are looking at the real scope, and I’ll tell you honestly whether it looks like a claim or wear.

Siding Replacement

### Siding Replacement That Actually Holds Up

New siding does two things at once: it transforms how your home looks and protects it from everything Ohio weather throws at it. Done right, it's an investment that lasts decades. Done wrong, you'll be dealing with warping, gaps, and moisture problems within a few years.

I install vinyl siding primarily using Polaris and Royal products — brands with real track records in the Midwest climate. Styles include traditional lap, dutch lap, shake, and board-and-batten depending on your home's architecture and your preferences. Every install includes house wrap and proper moisture management so the wall system performs correctly.

If your siding was damaged by hail, wind, or impact, I document it and meet your adjuster on the roof. I've helped hundreds of Cincinnati-area homeowners get siding replacements covered — the key is thorough documentation and knowing what adjusters look for. That's part of the job.

Questions & Answers

### Siding Replacement FAQ

What siding brands do you install?

I primarily install Polaris and Royal vinyl siding — both are well-tested in the Midwest climate and carry strong manufacturer warranties. I can discuss specific product lines and color options during your estimate.

How long does siding replacement take?

Most single-family homes take 2–4 days depending on size, style, and how much trim work is involved. I'll give you a realistic timeline before work starts.

Can hail damage get my siding covered by insurance?

Yes — hail damage is one of the most common covered perils for siding. The key is documentation. Joe will inspect and photograph every affected area to build a strong claim file before your adjuster comes out.

What's the difference between dutch lap, lap, and shake siding?

Traditional lap has a flat face with a slight overlap. Dutch lap has a curved notch cut into each panel for a more dimensional look. Shake mimics the look of wood shingle siding with a textured, staggered appearance. I can show you samples of each during the estimate.

Do you handle siding on two-story homes?

Yes. My crew and I have the equipment and experience for multi-story installations. Heights don't change the quality of the work — just the setup logistics.

Some of my siding is rotted. Do I have to replace all of it?

Usually not. Rot only travels as far as the water did, so localized damage to wood siding, fascia or soffit is normally a board repair rather than a re-side — and wood profiles are still milled, so a new board disappears under paint in a way a discontinued vinyl panel never will. Replacement starts making sense when the damage runs across a whole elevation, when the boards are too far gone to hold a fastener, or when you are changing the look of the house anyway.

What Homeowners Say

### Straight Talk From Real People

#### 🪵 Is it wood, not vinyl?

Everything above is about panel siding. If what is failing on your house is wood — rotted boards, soft fascia, broken soffit, cedar gone punky, window head trim drinking water — that is a different repair with a different method and a different price. Rot gets cut back to sound material and pieced in; there is no color match to chase.

Wood siding, fascia & soffit repair →

Questions & Answers

### Siding Repair FAQ

Can you match my existing siding color and style?

I do my best to source close matches. Exact matches depend on manufacturer availability and how much the existing siding has faded. I'll show you samples before any work starts so there are no surprises.

My siding has a few cracked panels — does that mean I need to replace all of it?

Not necessarily. If the underlying structure is solid and the damage is isolated, panel replacement is usually the right call. Joe will give you an honest assessment — not a pitch for a full job he doesn't think you need.

Does insurance cover siding repairs from a storm?

If the damage was caused by a covered weather event, yes. Hail and wind damage are frequently covered. The key is proper documentation of the damage. I handle that process regularly.

How long does a siding repair typically take?

Most targeted repairs take anywhere from a few hours to a full day depending on how much area is involved. I'll give you a realistic time estimate upfront.

Can loose or warped siding cause bigger problems if I ignore it?

Yes. Gaps and loose panels let moisture into the wall cavity, which can lead to insulation damage, mold, and eventually structural issues. It's worth getting it looked at sooner rather than later.

My siding is wood, not vinyl — do you repair that?

Yes, and it is a different job. Rotted wood gets cut back to sound material and pieced in, or packed and sanded flush where the rot is shallow, then primed and painted — there is no discontinued color to chase the way there is with a vinyl panel. That covers siding boards, fascia, soffit, corner boards, window and door head trim, and cedar or wood shake. One honest difference worth knowing up front: rot is usually not an insurance claim, because carriers exclude long-term moisture damage as maintenance.

Wood Siding Repair

### Rot Is Smaller Than It Looks.

Rot looks worse from the ground than it is. It travels exactly as far as the water did and no further — so the honest scope on most calls is a board or two, not a wall. I probe to find where sound wood starts and stops, cut back to solid material, and piece in new.

The part most people skip is the reason it rotted. A gutter seam running down the back of the fascia, a missing kick-out flashing, an open caulk joint at a window head, a downspout dumping against a corner board — fix the wood without fixing the water and you are doing it again in three years. Both get handled on the same visit.

Straight talk on insurance: rot is usually not a claim. Carriers exclude long-term moisture damage as wear and maintenance, and I would rather tell you that here than after you have filed. Storm damage to wood siding and trim is different — wind tearing a board loose, a limb through a wall, hail splitting trim — and that one I document and handle for you.

- Rotted board cut-out and replacement — cedar lap, painted clapboard, T1-11, board and batten
- Filler repair on shallow rot — packed, sanded flush, painted to blend
- Fascia board repair and replacement, including behind the gutter line
- Soffit board repair and replacement
- Wood trim, corner boards, and window and door head rot
- Cedar and wood shake repair and re-attachment
- Aluminum fascia wrap over sound wood, when you're done repainting it
- The water source found and fixed — gutter seam, kick-out, caulk joint, downspout
- New boards cut and painted on the ground before they go up
- Storm damage to wood siding and trim documented for your insurance claim
- NBD Lifetime Pledge on all repair work — NBD backed

What Homeowners Say

### Straight Talk From Real People

Questions & Answers

### Wood Siding Repair FAQ

What actually counts as wood siding repair?

Anything on the outside of your house made of wood that has gone soft, split, come loose or rotted through. That covers siding boards themselves — cedar lap, painted clapboard, T1-11 sheet, board and batten — plus fascia, soffit, corner boards, window and door head trim, and cedar or wood shake. It is the same skill set whether it is one board or a whole elevation, and most of what I get called for is one or two boards.

My house is vinyl. Why would I need wood repair?

Because vinyl walls still have wood behind and above them. On almost every home built in the last 35 years the fascia, soffit, corner boards and window heads are wood — the vinyl only covers the field of the wall. That wood is what rots, and it usually rots first, because it is where the gutters, the roof edge and the flashing all meet. If you are seeing paint peel or a dark stain along the roof line on a vinyl house, that is wood underneath and it is worth a look.

Where does rot usually start?

In the same handful of places, and once you know them you can check your own house from the driveway. Behind and below the gutters, where a leaking seam has been running down the back of the fascia for years. At the bottom course near grade, where splashback and mulch keep the wood damp. At window and door heads, where a failed caulk joint or missing flashing lets water in above the trim. On north-facing walls that never dry out. And wherever a downspout dumps against a corner board. Butt joints between boards are the other one — end grain drinks water.

Is it cheaper to repair rotted wood or just replace the siding?

Repair, in nearly every case where the rot is localized — and localized is what it usually is, because rot only travels as far as the water did. Replacement starts making sense when the damage is spread across a whole elevation, when the boards are so thin or cupped that new fasteners will not hold, or when you are already planning to change the look of the house. I will give you the honest read at the inspection, including when the answer is that you do not need me yet.

Do you paint the repair, or do I have to hire a painter after?

I paint it. New boards get cut and painted on the ground before they go up, and filler repairs get sanded flush and painted to blend into the existing finish. On a Montgomery job the rot had opened up through painted wood lap siding in two separate spots, and the finished repair takes some hunting to find. What I cannot promise is a perfect match to a wall that has been fading for fifteen years — if a full-side repaint is the honest answer, I will say so.

Can wood rot wait until spring?

Sometimes, and I will tell you when it can. A dry, shallow spot on a south-facing board with no path into the wall behind it can genuinely wait. What should not wait is anything open at a roof edge, a window head, or a butt joint — those are funnels, and a winter of freeze-thaw through an open cavity turns a board repair into a sheathing repair. If I look at yours and it can wait, that is what you will hear.

Gutter Replacement

### Seamless Gutters Built for Ohio Weather

Most gutter problems come from sectional gutters with too many joints. Every joint is a potential leak point, especially after Ohio winters expand and contract the metal repeatedly. Seamless gutters eliminate most of those failure points by running a single continuous piece from corner to downspout.

I custom-cut gutters on-site using a portable gutter machine — that means the metal is cut exactly to your home's dimensions, no approximations. I install 5-inch K-style for most residential applications and 6-inch where the roof pitch or drainage load requires it.

I also work with homeowners on storm-damaged gutters — if hail or wind crushed or tore your gutters loose, that's a common insurance claim. I document the damage and meet the adjuster the same way I do for roofing claims.

- Removal and disposal of old gutters and downspouts
- Custom-cut seamless aluminum gutters — fabricated on-site
- 5" K-style standard; 6" K-style available for higher load situations
- Downspout installation with proper drainage direction away from foundation
- Hidden hanger system installation for stronger support
- End caps, miters, and all necessary fittings
- Gutter guard and screen options — sized run-by-run, not sold by the sheet
- Damage documentation for storm-damaged gutters
- NBD Lifetime Pledge on all installation work

Guards & Screens

### What Failing Gutters Look Like. And When Guards Are Actually Worth It.

These are from my own camera roll — the conditions I find on inspections across Greater Cincinnati. Every one of them started as "we'll clean them next year."

An old screen doing nothing. Bent lip, spike backing out — water's been going behind this gutter, not through it.

One season of leaves, zero protection. The weight is already pulling this run off the fascia.

The end of that road. Rotted fascia and sagging soffit where a failed gutter used to be — now it's a carpentry job too.

How it starts. Grit, twigs, and the first oak leaves settling in between the hangers — this run hasn't overflowed yet. Yet.

Every hanger is a snag point. One twig clump like this backs water up behind it every time it rains hard.

And the other end of the story, from one of my jobs: expanded-metal screens seated flat along the run — leaves stay out, water gets in, and nobody's up on a ladder every November.

Here's my honest take on gutter guards and screens: they're not magic, and I won't sell them like they are. The right answer depends on what's hanging over your roof.

Heavy tree canopy overhead? Screens pay for themselves — cleaning and re-cleaning a clogged run costs more over a few years than protecting it once, and the photos above show where "we'll get to it" ends. Open sky? Skip the guards and put that money into the gutter system itself.

That's why I quote protection run by run — the tree-covered runs get screens, the open runs don't get padded onto your bill. If your existing screens are still good, I'll tell you that too, and reinstall them instead of replacing them. Fascia and sub-fascia wood replacement is included in my gutter pricing — however many boards it takes.

What Homeowners Say

### Straight Talk From Real People

Questions & Answers

### Gutter Replacement FAQ

What's the difference between seamless and sectional gutters?

Sectional gutters come in pre-cut pieces that are joined together with connectors. Seamless gutters run as one continuous piece from end to end, with joints only at corners and downspouts. Fewer joints means fewer places for leaks to develop over time.

What size gutters do most homes need?

5-inch K-style gutters handle most residential rooflines effectively. For steeper-pitched roofs, large roof sections, or areas with heavy tree coverage, 6-inch gutters move more water and reduce the chance of overflow during heavy rain.

Can I add gutter guards at the same time?

Yes — and installation at the same time as new gutters is the most efficient way to do it. I carry several styles of gutter guard and I'll walk you through the options and trade-offs during the estimate.

My gutters were damaged in a storm — is that covered by insurance?

Often yes. Hail and wind damage to gutters is a common covered claim. I'll inspect and document the damage and write the estimate; if there's a legitimate claim, you file it and I can meet the adjuster.

How often should gutters be replaced?

Well-maintained aluminum gutters typically last 20–25 years. Signs it's time to replace: visible sagging, pulling away from the fascia, persistent leaks at joints, or gutters crushed by ice or falling debris.

Gutter Cleaning

### Cleared By Hand. Tested, Not Assumed.

Most gutter cleaning calls I get come after somebody notices water pouring over the front edge during a hard rain, or a downspout that just isn't draining like it used to. The fix is straightforward, but doing it right takes actually clearing every run by hand — not blowing the loose stuff off the top and calling it done, which leaves the packed, decomposed debris sitting in the bottom of the trough exactly where it clogs the next downspout.

Every downspout gets a water flush-test once the run is clear, so I know for certain it drains free before I leave — not just that the trough looks empty from the ladder. You get a before/after photo report so you can see the work without climbing up yourself.

If I find something beyond ordinary debris while I'm up there — a sagging section, a loose fastener, a crushed or disconnected downspout — I show you and price it separately before doing anything about it. A routine cleaning call never turns into a bigger job without you seeing it and signing off first.

Questions & Answers

### Gutter Cleaning FAQ

How often do gutters actually need cleaning?

Twice a year is the standard — once after the trees drop leaves in fall, once in spring after the seed pods and helicopters come down. Heavy tree cover overhead can push that to three times a year. I'll tell you honestly what your specific setup needs, not just recommend the maximum.

Do you just blow it out with a leaf blower?

No — every run gets cleared by hand, not just blown around. A blower moves the loose stuff on top and leaves the packed, decomposed debris sitting in the bottom of the trough, which is exactly what clogs a downspout later. Hand-clearing gets all of it, not just what's visible from the ladder.

How do I know it's actually done and not just glanced at?

Every downspout gets flush-tested with water to confirm it drains free, and you get a before/after photo report when I'm done. You don't have to climb a ladder yourself to check the work.

Would gutter screens be a better option than ongoing cleaning?

Fair question, and it depends on your tree cover. Screens cut down how often you need a cleaning, but they don't eliminate it — fine grit and seed pods still get through most screen types over time. I can quote screens separately if that's the direction you want to go; I won't push a bigger job onto a routine cleaning call.

What if you find damage while you're up there?

I'll show you and price it separately before doing anything about it — a sagging section, a loose fastener, a crushed downspout, whatever it is. It never gets assumed into the cleaning price without you seeing it first.

How fast can you get out here?

Routine cleaning usually doesn't need a separate inspection visit first, so it often goes straight on the schedule — same-day or next-day in a lot of cases, depending on the week.

Interior Repair

### Prep Done Right Before Paint Goes On.

Most interior calls I get are the same handful of things: a crack across a ceiling, a gap that opened up at a corner, a tape joint that separated years after the drywall went up. None of it is dramatic, and none of it needs a full remodel — it needs someone to fill it, tape it, mud it and sand it flush so the surface is actually ready for paint instead of showing every seam through a fresh coat.

My interior crew handles it, and I'm on the job the same as I am for a roof. Plenty of these calls come from homeowners I'm already working with outside who ask me to look at something inside too. Furniture gets moved and reset as needed to reach every wall, and if I open up a crack and find something beyond surface-level — soft board, active moisture, real structural movement — I stop and show you before pricing anything extra.

Straight talk: ordinary settling cracks and aged joints usually aren't an insurance claim, the same way roof wear isn't. If a crack traces back to a real event — a leak, a burst pipe, storm damage — that's a different situation, and I'll tell you honestly which one you're in. When a roof leak is behind it, here's how I handle leak-damaged drywall and ceilings.

- Ceiling and wall crack, gap and separated-joint repair
- Re-tape and re-mud on seams that have lifted or cracked, feathered and sanded smooth
- Corner bead and corner seam repair
- Caulk at trim, corners, and transitions
- Light sanding to a uniform, paint-ready finish
- Furniture moved and reset as needed to reach every surface
- Full-room prep or targeted spot repairs — one crack or a whole ceiling
- Leak-damaged drywall and ceilings cut out and replaced, after the roof is fixed
- Paint on request — ask when you call what's included
- NBD Lifetime Pledge on all repair work — NBD backed

After a Roof Leak

### Fix the Roof First. Then the Ceiling.

A water stain on the ceiling is usually the first sign a roof has let go — and by the time it shows, the drywall behind it has often soaked through, sagged, or started coming apart at the seams. Patching over that doesn't hold. The wet board has to come out.

So I do it in the right order. First I find where the water is actually getting in and fix it — shingles, flashing, a pipe boot, whatever let go. There's no point hanging new drywall under a roof that's still leaking. Then my interior crew cuts out the damaged drywall or ceiling, replaces it, and tapes, muds and sands it smooth, ready for paint. One contact for both halves of the job — you're not hiring a roofer, then hunting down a drywall guy and explaining the whole thing twice.

If the leak came from storm damage, the interior damage can belong on the same insurance claim as the roof. I document the ceiling and walls right along with the roof so they don't get left off the scope — and I'll tell you straight if it isn't a claim.

If it turned into a bigger mess — standing water that needs extraction and dry-out, mold, or fire and smoke damage — that's large-scale mitigation, and I bring in United Restore for that part. Once it's dried out and cleaned up, my crew does the drywall and ceiling rebuild. More on that on the fire, water & smoke damage page.

- Leak source found and fixed first — shingles, flashing, pipe boots, whatever let the water in
- Water-damaged drywall and ceiling sections cut out and replaced
- Taped, mudded and sanded to blend with the surrounding surface, ready for paint
- Interior damage documented alongside the roof when it's part of an insurance claim
- United Restore brought in only when it needs dry-out, mold remediation, or fire/smoke cleanup

#### Still Leaking Right Now?

Stop the water first. If the roof is open or actively leaking, I can get it tarped so no more water reaches the ceiling while the permanent repair gets scheduled — see emergency roof tarping.

Then it's one job, in order: roof fixed, ceiling replaced, room ready for paint.

What Homeowners Say

### Straight Talk From Real People

Questions & Answers

### Interior Repair FAQ

Do you do interior work? I thought this was a roofing company.

Yes. Roofing, siding and gutters are most of what I do, but I have an interior crew for drywall and ceilings — everything from cracks, gaps and separated joints up to replacing drywall and ceilings that a roof leak soaked through. A lot of it comes up because I'm already fixing the roof that caused the stain, and it makes sense for one person to handle both.

What does an interior repair actually cover?

Two kinds of work. The everyday kind is cracks, gaps, and separated corner or joint seams on ceilings and walls — filling and finishing visible cracks, re-taping and re-mudding seams where the tape has lifted or cracked, caulking gaps at trim and transitions, and light sanding so the surface is uniform and paint-ready. The bigger kind is leak damage — cutting out drywall or ceiling that got soaked, replacing it, and finishing it to match. Either way it's repair, not a full remodel.

Do you paint after the repair?

Ask when you call — it depends on the job and what you want handled. Some homeowners want prep only and are doing their own cleaning, priming and painting; others want the whole thing off their plate. Either way, the scope gets written down before anyone starts, so there's no argument later about what was and wasn't included.

My ceiling has a water stain from a roof leak. Can you fix both?

Yes — and in that order. I find and fix where the water is getting in first, because new drywall under a roof that still leaks is money thrown away. Then my interior crew cuts out the damaged drywall or ceiling, replaces it, and finishes it ready for paint. You deal with me for both. If it's a bigger mess — standing water that needs to be dried out, mold, or fire and smoke damage — United Restore handles that mitigation first, then my crew does the rebuild.

What if you find something worse once you open up a crack?

I stop, show you what I found, and price it separately before going further. Most cracks are ordinary settling or a tape joint that let go over time. Occasionally opening one up reveals soft board, active moisture, or movement that points to something structural — and that's not a risk I price into a flat prep quote sight unseen. You'll always see it and sign off on it before it becomes extra work or extra cost.

Is a cracked ceiling or wall something insurance covers?

Ordinary settling cracks and aged tape joints usually aren't — that's wear and maintenance, the same way roof wear isn't a claim. Damage from a real event is different: if a storm-damaged roof let water in and ruined a ceiling, that interior damage can belong on the same claim as the roof, and I document the inside along with the roof. I'll tell you honestly which situation you're in rather than guess.

How big a job do you take? Is one room too small?

One room is a completely normal call. Most interior repair jobs I do are a single room or a handful of specific cracks and joints, not a whole-house remodel. Furniture gets moved and reset as needed to reach every wall, and the price reflects the actual room, not a minimum job fee padded to make it worth showing up.

Fire, Water & Smoke Damage

### When It's More Than a Roofing Job.

Some jobs go beyond a roof replacement. Fire damage, water intrusion, and smoke damage affect the entire structure — and navigating the insurance claim for full restoration is a completely different process than a standard storm claim.

I handle the exterior scope — roof, siding, gutters, fascia, soffit, decking — and my interior crew handles the drywall and ceilings inside. For the big mitigation work — water extraction and dry-out, mold remediation, fire and smoke cleanup — I bring in United Restore. Once they've dried it out and cleaned it up, my crew does the rebuild. That means you're not juggling separate contractors and separate estimates. I coordinate it. (More on the inside work on my interior repair page.)

If you've had a fire, a severe water intrusion, or smoke damage, the first call you make matters. I document the exterior damage scope immediately — before anything is disturbed — which protects your claim and ensures nothing gets missed by the adjuster.

- Immediate exterior damage assessment and documentation
- Full photo and written scope for insurance purposes
- Roof, siding, soffit, fascia, and structural decking review
- Direct coordination with United Restore for water extraction, dry-out, mold remediation, and fire/smoke cleanup
- Drywall and ceiling replacement by my interior crew once the space is dried out
- Single point of contact through the entire claim
- Supplement support if initial claim scope is incomplete

#### Why Documentation Timing Matters

Insurance adjusters are trained to minimize scope. The first 24-48 hours after a fire or major water event are critical — this is when damage is fully visible and before any temporary repairs disturb the evidence.

Joe shows up fast, documents everything, and makes sure your claim reflects the full reality of what happened — not just what the adjuster wants to write.

Roof Cleaning & Soft Wash

### Those Black Streaks Aren't Dirt. They're Eating Your Shingles.

The dark staining you see on roofs across Greater Cincinnati is Gloeocapsa magma — a type of algae that feeds on the limestone in your shingles. Left alone, it breaks down the granule layer, reduces reflectivity, and shortens your roof's lifespan by years.

Moss and lichen are even worse. They retain moisture against the shingle surface, work their roots into the mat, and cause the kind of damage that voids warranties and triggers premature replacement.

Joe uses a low-pressure soft wash system — not a pressure washer. High-pressure washing destroys granules and can void manufacturer warranties. Soft wash uses a biodegradable treatment solution applied at low pressure that kills the organism at the root and prevents regrowth for years.

- Low-pressure soft wash — safe for all shingle types
- Algae, moss, and lichen treatment and removal
- Black streak elimination (Gloeocapsa magma)
- Gutter flush included
- Biodegradable, plant-safe solution
- Pre and post inspection — catch any hidden damage while we're up there

#### Soft Wash vs. Pressure Wash

✓ SOFT WASH (What We Do)

Low pressure · Kills organism at root · Prevents regrowth · Won't void warranty · Safe for gutters and landscaping

✗ PRESSURE WASH (What We Don't)

Strips granules · Only removes surface staining · Damage returns in months · Can void GAF warranty

Inspected Before & After

We document condition before cleaning and check for hidden damage while we're up there

From My Drone — And My Ladder

### This Is What's Growing On Your Roof.

From the drone: algae streaking the shaded north plane while the far side of the same ridge stays clean. That asymmetry is the tell — it's growth, not dirt.

At arm's reach: moss wedged into the keyways, physically lifting the shingle edges — holding moisture against the mat every day it stays.

And here's the wash actually working — one frame, mid-treatment, from one of my jobs. The dark half is years of algae; the light half is the same roof minutes later, back to the color the homeowner paid for. No pressure washer touched it — the treatment does the work and the rain finishes the rinse.

Every shot above is from my own inspections and jobs around Greater Cincinnati. This is exactly the condition soft wash treats — killed at the root, rinsed by the rain, without a pressure washer stripping your granules.

FAQ

### Roof Cleaning Questions.

How often should a roof be cleaned?

In Greater Cincinnati's humid climate, most roofs benefit from cleaning every 3-5 years. North-facing slopes and roofs shaded by trees accumulate algae and moss faster and may need more frequent treatment.

Will soft wash damage my gutters or plants?

No. We use a biodegradable solution and rinse landscaping before and after application. The process is designed to be safe for everything around the house.

How long until I see results?

Black streaks from algae disappear within a few days as the dead organism rinses away with rain. Moss may take a few weeks to fully release from the surface.

Can you combine cleaning with an inspection?

Yes — and we recommend it. While Joe is up there cleaning, he does a full condition check. If there's any storm damage hiding under the staining, you'll know about it.

Sheds & Outbuildings

### The Job Plenty of Outfits Won't Schedule.

Plenty of outfits will not quote a shed. The job is too small to justify the setup, so the call gets a polite no — and homeowners tell me they heard it three or four times before they got to me. I schedule them. A shed roof is a half-day or a day, and the work is not different in kind from a house: strip it, look at the deck, dry it in, shingle it properly.

What is different is what these buildings have usually been through. An outbuilding is the thing on a property that goes longest without anyone looking at it, so the roof is often original, frequently rolled roofing, and the deck underneath has been quietly taking water for years. That is exactly why it gets torn off rather than covered over — you cannot inspect a deck through a layer you left in place.

If the house is due too, say so. The setup, the dump run and the mobilization are the fixed costs on a small roof, so an outbuilding folded into a house job costs less than the same shed done on its own.

- Full tear-off and re-roof — shed, detached garage, barn, pool house, lean-to
- Old rolled roofing stripped off, never shingled over
- Decking inspected with the roofing off, and rotted sheathing replaced
- Synthetic underlayment, starter course, and proper drip edge
- Architectural shingles — the same product that goes on a house
- Ridge cap, and old ridge vent closed back in where it is failing
- Leak and flashing repair where a re-roof is not warranted yet
- Rotted fascia, soffit and trim on the same visit
- Storm damage documented for a detached-structure insurance claim
- Old roofing bagged on tarps, and the site left clean
- NBD Lifetime Pledge on the work — NBD backed

What Homeowners Say

### Straight Talk From Real People

Questions & Answers

### Shed & Outbuilding Roofing FAQ

Will you actually re-roof a shed? A lot of places say no.

Yes. It is the most common thing I hear on these calls — somebody has phoned four companies and every one of them wanted a house-sized job or nothing. A shed is a half-day or a day, it needs the same tear-off, the same underlayment and the same flashing discipline as anything else, and I schedule it. Same for a detached garage, a barn, a pool house or a lean-to.

What does a shed roof usually cost?

Far less than a house, and I will give you the number before anything starts. For scale, the published jobs on this site run from about $1,500–$2,000 for a long ridge repair on a gambrel building up to $11,000–$12,000 for a whole property — house, attached garage and the detached outbuilding out back, all three done together. A single shed on its own sits at the small end of that. Free inspection either way.

Is it cheaper to do the shed at the same time as the house?

Usually, yes, and it is the main reason to think about them together. The setup, the dump run and the mobilization are the fixed costs on a small roof, so folding the outbuilding into a house job spreads them. On a New Richmond storm job the house and the outbuildings were stripped and dried in by morning and finished by mid-afternoon — same crew, same day, one setup.

My shed has rolled roofing on it. Can that just be shingled over?

I would not, and here is why. Old rolled roofing traps moisture against the deck, and going over it hides whatever the deck has been doing underneath. On a recent shed the roll came off and the decking under it was stained dark around the old fasteners — you only see that with the roofing off. Tear-off, look at the deck, then synthetic underlayment and shingles. Shingling over a problem is how a shed roof fails twice.

Does homeowners insurance cover a shed or detached garage roof?

Often, yes — most policies cover detached structures under a separate limit, usually a percentage of the dwelling coverage, and storm damage to an outbuilding is a real claim. It is also the part carriers most often leave out of a scope. On a New Richmond job the carrier approved part of the claim and denied the rest, which is where most homeowners stop; we worked the rest of it and then did the whole job. If a storm hit your shed, it is worth having me document it.

Do you do more than the roof on an outbuilding?

Yes — rotted fascia and soffit, trim, and wood siding repair go with this work more often than not, because an outbuilding is usually the thing on the property that has gone longest without attention. If your shed needs the roof and the trim, that is one visit, not two.

The Real Math

### Don't Shrink the Project. Shrink the Payment.

Here's the trap I watch homeowners fall into every year: the roof needs $14,000 of work, the checking account says $2,000 — so the $2,000 patch wins. Not because it solves anything. Because it's what today's cash can reach. When a repair genuinely fixes it, I'll quote you the repair and shake your hand. But on a roof that's at the end of its life, patch money is rent, not equity. It buys months. It never counts toward the roof you'll still have to buy.

Sized to today's cash

$350–$2,500 per patch, per visit

The patch-and-pray plan on a roof that's already done.

- Fixes the leak you can see — the next weak spot is already forming
- Another storm season, another visit, another check

- Interior damage risk keeps compounding while you wait
